verdict.why:
I wrote my own classifier from the test wording, without using ledger.mjs or shape-meanings.mjs, and ran it over all 21,626 routes. Scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mashiachsonyosef-github-io/c72302ec-11e7-5b6d-a5ab-47bb077585fe/scratchpad/punct/verify/ubs_sdbh_hebrew_v0_9_2/: lib.mjs, verify.mjs, falsify.mjs, probe2.mjs, compare.mjs, labels.mjs, and the *.out.json files.

What reproduces:
- The inventory matches exactly: 41 marks, 58,686 occurrences.
- All 11 ';' shapes reproduce exactly.
- The ';' falsifier count of 25 reproduces.
- (d) The v3 comparison reproduces exactly, using my own depth-0 ';' pack followed by the imported senseSplit. Of 21,626 fields: 10,516 same, 11,108 where v3 divides and the declaration keeps whole, 0 where only the declaration divides, 0 divided differently, 2 where v3 prints nothing. senseSplit alone gives 18,320, 3,296 and 10. Pills: 44,078 in all, 32,530 not the route, 8,604 opening with a note marker, 'man' 2,894 times, and 40 also a route on the key (case-insensitive; 37 exact). The '8,048 pills with a label' figure does not reproduce: the draft never defines 'label', and my readings give 3,843 to 8,540 (labels.mjs).

(a) Counts as the tests are worded (verify.asworded.out.json): 24 shape counts differ.
- The dividing comma shapes come out at elliptic 26 instead of 15 and complete 7 instead of 9. The cause is that the appositive word list ends in '...' and the complete test counts words inside parentheses.
- With 12 amendments that the data forces (see corrections) and a stated order of shapes within each mark, every count reproduces except comma.series_item (1,765 vs 1,759) and comma.definition_prose (4,842 vs 4,848). Those are 6 commas between two non-dividing shapes (verify.amended.out.json).
- comma.series_item_closed_by_conjunction_without_comma reaches 108 under only one of my readings of its test; the others give 68 or 155.

(b) Completeness as worded: 15 occurrences fall into no shape. All of them are ◄ or ►: 11 after ) ” : . or =, and 4 ► after ׃. Also, 17 pairs of tests overlap, for example 39 commas match both before_conjunction and series_item, and the declaration states no order among shapes within a mark. With the amendments, nothing is left unexplained.

(c) Falsification of the dividing shapes:
- semicolon.before_alternative_label is plainly wrong at 3 of its 26 occurrences, and the draft neither states nor counts these. In each, ';' before 'either:' follows a hedge head and opens the FIRST alternative. There is no earlier meaning for it to replace, and the alternation is carried by a later '; or' (present in all 3): קנה «meaning unsure; either: (1) = type of gra…», חשש «meaning unsure; either: (1) = dried grass…», דבר «exact meaning uncertain; either: = the act of spea…». The other 23 hold.
- Elliptic (15), complete (9), name_variant (4), comma.before_alternative_label (2) and exclamation.between_interjections (2) survived at least 3 attempts each. פיה «mouth of well, cave, pit» and אח «brother! alas!» are arguable but not plainly wrong.

Non-dividing shapes whose meaning fails (falsified_meanings): unlabeled alternatives under semicolon.before_or_clause, packed literal renderings under comma.definition_prose, and two packed renderings under comma.short_route_appositive. None of these changes what is printed, because the declaration ships every route whole. But they contradict the ledger's claims that ';' is "never two readings" except when labeled, and that a comma packs renderings "only in a short marker-free route".
falsified_meanings: semicolon.before_alternative_label (dividing, 26): 3 counterexamples, none stated or counted. ';' before 'either:' closes a hedge head and opens the first alternative, so it does not introduce 'a second meaning in place of the one before it'. Keys: קנה «meaning unsure; either: (1) = type of gra…», חשש «meaning unsure; either: (1) = dried grass…», דבר «exact meaning uncertain; either: = the act of spea…». In all 3 a later '; or' carries the alternation (probe2.out.json either_first).

semicolon.before_or_clause (non-dividing, 21; meaning 'adds a further referent or form inside one definition'): 6 plainly unlabeled alternatives offered in place of the first. The ';' falsifier says the census found none it could name; these name them: האטד and אטד «or possibly a thorny bush of the Rubus genus, which inclu…»; סנה «or perhaps this is a generic word for shrub»; זמרי «or possibly a substitution cipher, where the letters of t…»; סומפניה «or, a large drum; or a term referring to the whole ensemb…» (2 occurrences). 6 more are arguable second senses: דג and דגה «or, in a loosely sense, any of various other aquatic anim…»; עבד «or someone who presents himself as such when speaking to …»; מרא, מרה and אדון «or a person or deity who is referred to as such in a conv…».

comma.definition_prose (non-dividing; meaning 'apposition, modifier, clause ... inside one definition'): 69 depth-0 commas inside a 'literally:' segment pack literal renderings (probe2.mjs). 26 of them pass the draft's own packed_renderings_complete test, e.g. פקדה «literally: office, position; hence: = a spec…», קורה «literally: beam, rafter; hence: = covering…», מום «literally: blemish, defect; hence: = state in…». The rest are elliptic-like, e.g. רמם and רום «literally: to be, become high; hence: = pro…», קרא «literally: to call, summon; hence: = causativ…». This falsifies the declaration's claim that only a short marker-free route can carry a comma that packs renderings.

comma.short_route_appositive (non-dividing, 75; meaning 'joins a short definition to its apposition ... not two readings'): אתמול and תמל «(what used to be done) before, in the past» give two renderings of one sense, the same kind as 'joy, delight' (2 occurrences). חום «to have a dark, if not black, skin color» (first comma) opens an interruption, not an apposition; it is non-dividing, but filed under the wrong shape.

semicolon.before_hedged_meaning (non-dividing, 507; meaning 'follows a head that says the meaning is unsure'): in 24 the head says nothing of uncertainty, e.g. סינים «location; possibly Syene, town in E…» and ברד «location; ◄ near Kadesh; probably with cold water» (falsify.out.json N2). This is a wording problem: these are still one entry.

back_arrow.after_semicolon test text: 'or the sof pasuq the provider once uses for it' is wrong. ׃ occurs 4 times, always before ►, never before ◄: שלה, שילו, שילה, שלו «son of Judah׃ ► regarded as father of inha…». The draft counts those 4 under forward_arrow.after_semicolon, whose test names only ';'.
corrections: semicolon.before_alternative_label: move the 3 '; either:' that follow a hedge head (קנה, חשש, דבר) into a non-dividing shape, such as semicolon.before_hedged_meaning or a new semicolon.before_first_alternative. The dividing count then becomes 23, and the ';' divides_readings line '26 of 15,999' becomes 23.

semicolon.before_or_clause: split out the unlabeled alternatives (האטד, אטד, סנה, זמרי, סומפניה x2; and decide דג, דגה, עבד, מרא, מרה, אדון) as divides in meaning, not separated. Revise the ';' means text ('never two readings ... the one exception is labeled') and its falsifier ('found none it could name').

comma: add a shape for packed literal renderings inside a 'literally:' segment (69 by probe2.mjs; 26 complete-shaped), marked divides in meaning, not separated. Correct region_dependent: a comma can pack renderings in a definition's literal half, not only in short marker-free routes.

comma.short_route_appositive: state the full word list. Reproducing 75/15/9/6/2 needs at least: suitable, probably, possibly, destroyed, selectively, lined, if, capable. Without them, 11 more commas would be declared dividing (elliptic 26). Refile אתמול and תמל «before, in the past» as packed renderings (2), and the first comma of חום as an interruption opener.

comma.short_route_packed_renderings_complete: state that words and function words are counted outside parentheses. Without that, טחורים «(images of) hemorrhoids, tumors, ulcers» (2 commas) falls to elliptic, giving complete 7 and elliptic 26.

comma.series_item_closed_by_conjunction_without_comma: state the test exactly. Only the reading 'the rest of the clause has no comma and and/or comes after 1-3 words' gives 108; other readings give 68 or 155. comma.series_item and comma.definition_prose still differ by 6 under my best reading (1,765 vs 1,759; 4,842 vs 4,848), so state how words are counted (whitespace tokens or letter tokens).

comma.label_punctuation reaches 157 only if ', hence:' (צפין) is counted and ', possible:' (או «exact meaning unknown, possible: =») is not. Both stand before a label, so either count both (158) or explain the difference.

forward_arrow.after_semicolon: add ׃ to the test (4). back_arrow.after_semicolon: drop the sof pasuq clause. back_arrow and forward_arrow inline_without_punctuation: the test says 'after a word', but 11 occurrences follow ) ” : . or = (◄: כרפס, הובנים, הבנים, תפוח, תפח, חמץ; ►: עזרה, יד, עזר, מלבן, קול). Reword the test or add shapes; as worded, 15 arrows fall into no shape.

Provider spellings missing from the tests: colon.after_literally needs 'liteallly' (רגז); equals.after_label_word_without_colon needs 'unkown' (בעים, עים); paren slot_placeholder needs "someone else's" (16 groups, so 16 '(' and 16 ')'); paren number_or_date needs 'c.' (יהוא '(c. 841-814)'); paren cross_reference must exclude the empty '(see )' (נתיבה, נחשתן); slash.pronoun_pair takes both slashes of 'his/her/their' (חליפה).

State the order of shapes within each mark. 17 pairs of tests overlap, e.g. comma before_conjunction & series_item 39, colon before_definition_equals & after_alternative_label 18, equals after_label_colon & between_phrase 3,966, period abbreviation & route_final 26. Exactly-one-shape holds only under an unstated order.

The v3 note's '8,048 pills open with a label' does not reproduce without a stated definition of 'label' (my readings give 3,843 to 8,540). The '113 of 120' for '>' gives 114 under my definition of a key carrying a 'literally:' route. Define both.

questions: Q1. A gloss route that packs two or three renderings with a comma (or two interjections with '!'), e.g. עצבה 'pain, trouble', לבוא 'to go, to arrive', חיא 'to be, become happy', יהב 'come on! hey!': one reading or several? Reading A (declared): one reading, the provider wrote one gloss and the owner ruled a comma in UBS is not different entries; 27 routes. Reading B: separate only where every piece stands alone: 8 routes would print 17 pills; 13 elliptic routes ('to be, become happy', 'mouth of well, cave, pit') stay whole because a cut would print 'to be'; 4 name-variant routes ('Ephrathah, Ephrath', 'inhabitant of Maacah, Maacath') and 2 interjection routes need their own answer. Evidence: the provider's normal second gloss is a second route (3,595 mark-free glosses of at most four words); in 3 of 9 complete packed commas a piece is also its own route on the key (לבוא writes 'to go' and 'to arrive' separately too).

Q2. A definition offering a labeled second meaning ('meaning unknown; possibly: = musical term; or: = musical instrument; or: = melody; ≈ ...', שמיני/עלמה/גתית, דבר, קנה, חשש): one reading or one per alternative? Reading A (declared): one record, since the head and trailing note belong to every alternative; 17 routes (26 semicolons). Reading B: cut at '; or:' / '; either:' / '; alternatively', leaving the head on the first piece and the note on the last; 17 routes. Also: 20 more routes carry an unlabeled '; or ...' / '; either ...' clause (21 semicolons), mostly a further referent ('; or a person or deity who is referred to as such') and sometimes an alternative identification ('; or possibly a thorny bush'); labeled alternatives also occur after ',' (2) and once after a period ('booths. Or alternatively, olive tree').

Q3. An idiom gloss 'literal > meaning' ('to see the light > to live', 'to hunt down > to oppress'): one reading or two? Reading A (declared): one gloss for one lexical meaning, matching the provider's 'literally: ...; hence: = ...' definitions (113 of the 120 sit on a key carrying one); 120 routes. Reading B: two readings, literal and meaning, cut at ' > ': 120 routes would print 240 pills. In 6 of the 120, one side is also written as its own gloss route on the key.

Q4. A definition with notes ('man; ◄ son of Heman; ► temple singer; time of king David'): is the head a reading? Reading A (declared): the record prints whole as one reading, notes included, with no head or note alone as a pill; 5,943 routes have a ';' before a note marker (7,674 carry a note marker at all). Reading B: cut at the first ';' before ◄ ► ≈ and print the head as the pill with the notes as notes, not pills. That keeps both pieces but makes 'man' (2,547 heads), 'town' (386) and 'woman' (126) readings of proper names. Today's card does more than either: every ';' piece is a pill, so 8,604 pills open with a note marker, 8,048 open with a label ('hence: = ...'), and 'man' prints alone 2,894 times.

Engine note for the owner: the task describes v3 as dividing at depth-0 semicolons and then commas. sense-split-v1.mjs's senseSplit only divides at commas. The ';' step is gloss-store-v1.mjs packSplit and the engine's own senseSplit. The primary comparison follows the card (';' then ','), and compare.json also reports senseSplit alone.
